The error occurs because style_paths is a set, and they attempt to .remove("do_not_save") assuming that there's a placeholder path added somewhere. But at initialization style_paths includes default_path and any style.path values. The placeholder "do_not_save" is used as path for divider entries: in reload(), they add style entry with path "do_not_save". Indeed in reload(), they add PromptStyle(name=divider, ... path="do_not_save". So style_paths should contain "do_not_save". However they added to style_paths only if style.path exists and is truthy: they loop through self.styles items, adding style.path if style.path. Since "do_not_save" is a string, it's truthy, so will be added.

But the error shows that "do_not_save" not in style_paths set, so .remove raises KeyError. Why missing? Possibly because there are no divider entries -> no style with path "do_not_save". That may happen if the default path is a file e.g., styles.csv (no "*") so reload() loads only that CSV and does not add dividers. In that case there would be no entries with path "do_not_save". But they still try to remove it. The logic should be safer: .discard instead of .remove, or check existence.

Thus fix: replace style_paths.remove("do_not_save") with style_paths.discard("do_not_save") (which doesn't raise error if absent). Also same for get_style_paths earlier lines (line 175). Indeed there is earlier function get_style_paths with same .remove. Should also use discard.
